articles.title: Telangana tops nation in alcohol use, 44% of men report drinking
articles.summary: NFHS-6: Telangana tops large states in alcohol use, with 43.9% of men and 7.1% of women drinking; rural rates higher than urban, sales rising.
articles.body: HYDERABAD: Telangana has once again emerged as the country’s highest alcohol-consuming large state, with nearly one in every two adult men reporting alcohol use, according to the latest National Family Health Survey (NFHS-6). The findings underline the state’s persistent lead over the rest of the country and point to a strong rural consumption pattern that continues to drive the numbers.As many as 43.9% of men aged 15 years and above in Telangana reported consuming alcohol in NFHS-6, more than double the national average of 18.9%. Despite a marginal decline from the previous survey round, Telangana has retained its position at the top among larger states.In NFHS-5, 50% of men aged 15-49 years in Telangana reported consuming alcohol, compared with the national average of 22.4%. While the age groups covered in the two surveys differ, the data indicate that Telangana has consistently remained well above the national average.Among major states, Rajasthan followed Telangana with 42.2% of men reporting alcohol consumption, while Chhattisgarh stood at 38.3%. Telangana’s figure was 1.7 percentage points higher than Rajasthan’s and 5.6 percentage points above Chhattisgarh’s. The gap with the national average was even more striking at 25 percentage points.The survey also highlights a pronounced rural-urban divide within the state. Alcohol consumption was reported by 46.6% of rural men, compared with 36.3% of urban men. The 10.3 percentage-point difference suggests that rural Telangana is the primary driver of the state’s high overall consumption rate.A similar trend is visible among women, although at much lower levels. Telangana recorded alcohol consumption among 7.1% of women aged 15 years and above, sharply higher than the national average of 1.1%. Only Rajasthan, at 19.9%, reported a significantly higher proportion among women, while Chhattisgarh stood at 5.7%.The rural-urban gap among women was even wider. While 8.6% of rural women reported consuming alcohol, the corresponding figure in urban areas was just 2.8%.The NFHS findings come against the backdrop of Telangana’s expanding liquor market. Liquor sales in the state touched around ₹40,209 crore in 2025-26, up from ₹37,487 crore in the previous financial year. Sales volumes also rose, with 382.91 lakh cases sold during 2025-26 compared with 372.25 lakh cases in 2024-25.Excise collections have mirrored this growth. Revenue from liquor sales was reported at about ₹39,368 crore, while total excise collections crossed ₹44,000 crore, highlighting the scale of the state’s alcohol market.While the NFHS data measure the proportion of people who report consuming alcohol rather than the quantity consumed, the survey nevertheless reinforces Telangana’s position as the country’s leading large state in terms of the prevalence of alcohol consumption, particularly in rural areas.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Hyderabad | Silver Rate in Hyderabad | Bank Holidays in Hyderabad | Public Holidays in Hyderabad | Hyderabad AQI | Weather in Hyderabad | Petrol Price in Hyderabad | Diesel Price in Hyderabad | CNG Price in Hyderabad | LPG Price in HyderabadStay updated with the latest Hyderabad news. articles.title: Veja como foram as campanhas dos candidatos ao governo de Roraima  | G1
articles.standfirst: Disputam o cargo os candidatos Arthur Henrique (PL), Soldado Sampaio (Republicanos), Rosi Aires (PSOL), Farah Mesquita (Solidariedade) e Clébio Genuíno (PCO). Eleições de 2026 ocorrem neste domingo (4).
articles.summary: Após 49 dias de campanha, candidatos ao governo de Roraima encerram agendas para as Eleições de 2026, que ocorrem neste domingo (4).
articles.body:
Candidados ao governo de Roraima que fizeram camapanha nas ruas: Arthur Henrique (PL), Soldado Sampaio (Republicanos) e Rosi Aires (PSOL) — Foto: Reprodução/Instagram

Os candidatos ao governo de Roraima chegaram à reta final das Eleições 2026 após 49 dias de campanha com agendas distribuídas de formas diferentes pelo estado. Arthur Henrique (PL) percorreu os 13 municípios do interior. Soldado Sampaio (Republicanos) visitou ao menos 10 regiões e dividiu os compromissos eleitorais com a agenda de governador interino . Rosi Aires (PSOL) também esteve em 10 municípios, além da capital Boa Vista .

Neste ano, também disputam o governo Farah Mesquita (Solidariedade) e Clébio Genuíno (PCO). Os dois, no entanto, tiveram poucas ações públicas de campanha. Farah concentrou as atividades em publicações nas redes sociais. Clébio informou ao g1 que não era mais candidato, mas o nome dele segue como "concorrendo" no sistema do Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE).

A campanha também marcou a continuidade de uma disputa iniciada em junho. Arthur Henrique e Soldado Sampaio concorreram ao governo na eleição suplementar realizada no dia 21. Arthur obteve 60% dos votos válidos , mas o resultado não foi definido pela Justiça Eleitoral porque o registro da candidatura estava sub judice. Sampaio ficou em segundo, com 35% .

Agora, os dois voltam a disputar o governo de Roraima ao lado de outros três candidatos. Nas duas pesquisas Quaest encomendadas pela Rede Amazônica, Arthur e Sampaio aparecem à frente dos demais candidatos.

Arthur Henrique registrou 60% das intenções de voto na primeira pesquisa e 57% na segunda . Sampaio tinha de 27% na primeira, e ficou com 32% na segunda.

Veja, abaixo, um resumo de como foi a campanha de cada candidato , na ordem apresentada na última pesquisa Quaest:

Durante a campanha, Arthur Henrique percorreu os 13 municípios do interior de Roraima , participou de caminhadas e reuniões, concedeu entrevistas, foi ao debate da Rede Amazônica , e se reuniu com outros candidatos e apoiadores. O candidato não foi em Normandia, como havia feito na campanha da eleição suplementar.

Ex-prefeito da capital pelos últimos cinco anos , Arthur concentrou a campanha no interior do estado, onde visitou vilas e comunidades, e teve o apoio do ex-governador Antonio Denarium . Ele tem como candidato a vice o empresário Haroldo Cathedral (Novo) e fez a campanha com o slogan " bora resolver ".

Além disso, também participou de um comício em Boa Vista ao lado do candidato a presidente do país Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), e dos candidatos ao Senado por Roraima e colegas de partido, Nicoletti e Hélio Fernando Barbosa Lopes , conhecido como Hélio Bolsonaro.

Entre as principais propostas do candidato, estão a recuperação de estradas vicinais e a substituição de pontes de madeira por estruturas de concreto no estado.

"Nós vamos implantar o maior programa de recuperação de vicinais da história do estado. É fazer um trabalho bem feito. É o governador olhando de perto, como nós fizemos em Boa Vista", declarou o candidato após detalhar os problemas de escoamento no interior.

Para a Saúde, ele prometeu criar um gabinete do governador dentro do Hospital Geral de Roraima (HGR), a maior unidade de alta complexidade do estado. A ideia dele é acompanhar de perto a rotina dos profissionais e identificar os gargalos operacionais nos centros cirúrgicos.

O candidato também disse que pretende modernizar o atendimento com a implantação de um prontuário eletrônico unificado. A ferramenta tem o objetivo de substituir os registros em papel, dar transparência às filas de espera por cirurgias e facilitar a realização de mutirões com especialistas contratados temporariamente.

Também falou substituir pontes de madeira por concreto no estado e investir em ensino médio técnico .

No último dia de campanha, nessa quinta-feira (1º), Arthur Henrique fez publicações nas redes sociais pedindo votos para candidatos do PL à Câmara dos Deputados e à Assembleia Legislativa.

Ele encerrou o dia com uma caminhada na praça do bairro Pérola, na zona Oeste, ao lado de apoiadores como o vice, da esposa, Nathália Cortez, Denarium e o atual prefeito da capital, Marcelo Zeitoune (PL) e Hélio Lopes. Arthur concorre na coligação " Unidos Por Roraima ", que reúne os partidos PL e Novo.

Sampaio dividiu a agenda de campanha com os compromissos como governador interino. Ele cumpriu agendas nos municípios do Cantá, Caracaraí, Caroebe, Iracema, Mucajaí, Normandia, Rorainópolis, São João da Baliza, São Luiz do Anauá e Uiramutã, conforme compromissos oficiais enviados à Rede Amazônica. Não há registros de visitas dele Alto Alegre, Amajari, Bonfim e Pacaraima.

Além disso, durante a campanha, disse várias vezes ser de direita e fez campanha ao lado de senadora Damares Alves (Republicanos-DF) em vista dela a Roraima. Ele não participou do comício de Flávio Bolsonaro em Boa Vista.

Ele tem como candidata a vice a ex-deputada federal, Shéridan Ramos (Podemos). O candidato afirmou várias vezes nos compromissos de campanha que é o " Soldado do Povo ".

A maior parte das agendas de campanha do candidato ocorreu na capital. Ele também participou das entrevistas promovidas pela Rede Amazônica e do debate entre os candidatos. Sampaio está há 154 dias no comando do estado, e esse período de gestão foi citado em diferentes eventos de campanha.

"Em 100 dias, eu já fiz muito mais pela saúde da nossa gente do que eles fizeram", disse o governador nas redes sociais.

Entre as propostas apresentadas pelo candidato durante a campanha, estão a criação de uma rede de monitoramento nas fronteiras com uso de tecnologia e a realização de palestras em escolas e igrejas para combater a violência contra a mulher .

Em entrevista à Rede Amazônica , também abordou a regularização fundiária e a gestão de terras, a ampliação de benefícios sociais para movimentar o comércio local, a realização de concursos públicos para as áreas de segurança, saúde e educação e o apoio à regulamentação federal do garimpo operado por cooperativas no estado.

Também disse que pretende promover ações de combate a entrada de facções no estado pelas áreas de fronteira e implantar o programa "Bolsa Macuxi", para combate a evasão escolar.

No último dia de campanha, nessa quinta, Sampaio participou de reuniões políticas de apoiadores, como os candidatos a deputado estadual Dr. Claudio Cirurgião (Republicanos) e Cláudio da Xarme (Podemos), em Boa Vista. Ele encerrou o dia em uma reunião política organizada por ele e pela candidata ao Senado Helena da Asatur (PSD).

Sampaio concorre com a coligação " Roraima Segue em Frente ", composta pelos partidos Republicanos, Podemos, Agir, PSD e Federação União Progressista.

Durante a campanha, a candidata concentrou as agendas em municípios e comunidades indígenas das regiões da Terra Indígena Raposa Serra do Sol e do Baixo São Marcos. Ela apoia e faz campanha para o atual presidente e candidato à reeleição, Lula (PT).

Ele participou de compromissos nos municípios de Amajari, Normandia, Rorainópolis, São Luiz do Anauá, Bonfim, Alto Alegre, Mucajaí, Iracema, Cantá e Boa Vista. Não há registros dela em Caracaraí, Caroebe, Pacaraima, São João da Baliza e Uiramutã.

Na capital, Rosi focou a campanha em bairros da periferia, como Senador Hélio Campos, Laura Moreira, Cruviana e Equatorial, na zona Oeste.

Além disso, também participou de encontros de apoio à agricultura familiar, conversas com camponesas do lavrado, panfletagens, entrevistas e visitas a apoiadores.

Rosi defende a captação de recursos diretamente junto ao Governo Federal para reestruturar a rede física das unidades de saúde do estado. Na área ambiental, disse ser contra o garimpo ilegal e argumentou que a atividade contamina rios e destrói terras indígenas.

"Defendo os programas sociais e de governo do presidente Lula. Na saúde, o Mais Médicos, o Samu e as UPAs. Na educação, o Pé-de-Meia, as escolas técnicas e as universidades", disse.

A candidata também propôs a criação da Universidade Federal Indígena em Uiramutã e a expansão do ensino intercultural bilíngue. Rosi disse ainda ser favorável à ampliação legal de áreas protegidas e indígenas, à transparência nas contas públicas e ao combate à corrupção.

A vice na chapa dela é Lúcia Patamona (PSOL). As duas concorrem na coligação "Roraima da Esperança", composta pela Federação Brasil da Esperança (PT/PCdoB/PV) e Federação PSOL Rede (PSOL e Rede).

Roraima tem 401.496 pessoas aptas a votar nas eleições deste ano . No estado, eleitores vão às urnas para escolher o presidente da República, o governador, dois senadores, oito deputados federais e 24 deputados estaduais, responsáveis por tomar decisões e elaborar leis que impactam a população entre 2027 e 2030 (e até 2035 no caso dos senadores).

O Senado vai renovar 54 das 81 cadeiras (dois terços do total). E cada eleitor deve votar em dois candidatos diferentes.

articles.title: Guerra no Irã pode reduzir emissões em 2026, mas queda ainda é incerta | G1
articles.standfirst: Revisões feitas após o início do conflito apontam queda de cerca de 0,5% nas emissões de CO₂ dos combustíveis fósseis. Histórico mostra que recuos em anos de crise costumam ser pequenos e temporários.
articles.summary: Queda na demanda por petróleo e gás mudou as projeções para 2026. Recuo estimado é pequeno, pode ser temporário e não interrompe o aumento de CO₂ na atmosfera.
articles.body:
Foto: Ria Puskas / Unsplash / Divulgação

A guerra no Irã provocou uma mudança inesperada nas projeções para as emissões globais de dióxido de carbono (CO₂) em 2026.

Depois de começar o ano prevendo crescimento, estimativas atualizadas da Agência Internacional de Energia (IEA) passaram a indicar uma pequena queda nas emissões associadas ao uso de petróleo, gás e carvão.

A redução projetada é de cerca de 0,5% em relação a 2025 , segundo uma análise do Carbon Brief, site britânico especializado em mudanças climáticas, baseada nas previsões da agência.

Em volume, isso representa aproximadamente 190 milhões de toneladas de CO₂ a menos.

O número é relevante porque quedas nas emissões globais de combustíveis fósseis são raras . Mas também exige cautela: o recuo corresponde a uma fração pequena das quase 40 bilhões de toneladas de CO₂ emitidas anualmente pela queima de carvão, petróleo e gás.

Além disso, a estimativa ainda é uma projeção para o conjunto de 2026, e pode mudar de acordo com a duração do conflito , os preços da energia e a recuperação do fornecimento de combustíveis nos próximos meses.

📉 As emissões fósseis podem terminar 2026 cerca de 0,5% abaixo de 2025.

🛢️ O petróleo concentra boa parte da mudança: a previsão da IEA passou de crescimento da demanda no início do ano para uma redução de cerca de 2,5 milhões de barris por dia em setembro.

🔥 O gás também perdeu espaço nas projeções, após restrições de oferta e preços mais altos.

🪨 O carvão segue na direção oposta: o consumo global deve crescer e atingir um novo recorde neste ano.

🌡️ Uma queda anual nas emissões, contudo, não significa queda do CO₂ na atmosfera. O mundo continuaria emitindo dezenas de bilhões de toneladas e aumentando a concentração do gás.

Os dados da Agência Internacional de Energia (IEA), checados pelo g1 , mostram como a projeção mudou ao longo do ano. O movimento foi apontado primeiro pelo Carbon Brief e depois destacado em uma análise do jornal “The Washington Post”.

Projeção global de emissões — Foto: Arte/g1

Em janeiro, a projeção indicava que as emissões associadas aos combustíveis fósseis ficariam 281 milhões de toneladas acima das de 2025.

A revisão da demanda por petróleo virou esse resultado para 260 milhões de toneladas abaixo. Depois, a nova previsão para o gás aprofundou o recuo para 454 milhões de toneladas abaixo de 2025.

O aumento projetado do carvão compensou parte dessa redução. Com isso, a estimativa mais recente aponta para um saldo de aproximadamente 191 milhões de toneladas de CO₂ a menos que em 2025.

A diferença entre a expectativa feita em janeiro e a projeção atual chega, portanto, a cerca de 472 milhões de toneladas de CO₂ .

⚠️ Isso, contudo, também não significa que 472 milhões de toneladas deixaram efetivamente de ser emitidas. O número mostra quanto a previsão para o ano mudou desde janeiro.

Essa distinção é importante porque parte da mudança resulta de previsões feitas antes da guerra que não se confirmaram, e não apenas de uma redução absoluta do consumo já registrada.

A queda na demanda global por petróleo ajudou a reduzir as projeções de emissões para 2026, mas o efeito pode ser pequeno e temporário. — Foto: REUTERS/Dado Ruvic/Ilustração

As emissões de CO₂ provenientes de combustíveis fósseis e da indústria vem aumentando desde a Revolução Industrial e passaram de cerca de 22,5 bilhões de toneladas em 1992 para 38,6 bilhões em 2024.

Nesse intervalo, houve poucos recuos relevantes. Depois da crise financeira internacional, as emissões caíram em 2009, mas voltaram a crescer rapidamente no ano seguinte.

Em 2020, a pandemia de Covid-19 provocou uma redução muito maior, seguida também por uma recuperação.

Por isso, segundo especialistas, uma eventual queda em 2026 não permite concluir, por enquanto, que as emissões globais entraram em uma trajetória permanente de redução.

Claudio Angelo, coordenador de política internacional do Observatório do Clima, diz que o principal cuidado é não confundir uma mudança conjuntural no mercado de energia com uma transformação estrutural do sistema energético .

“Pode até ser que as emissões fiquem meio estáveis, ou tenha uma pequena queda nesse ano por causa disso. Mas não é isso que vai resolver a mudança climática", afirma.

Para Angelo, o aspecto mais relevante da crise pode aparecer menos no resultado de um único ano e mais nas decisões que governos, empresas e consumidores tomarem diante dos preços altos e das dificuldades de abastecimento.

“Mais do que ficar olhando para a tonelada de carbono que reduziu aqui e ali, você precisa olhar para o que a guerra está fazendo com os mercados de energia mundo afora.”

O choque provocado pelo conflito atingiu principalmente o petróleo e o gás. Com interrupções no fornecimento e preços mais altos, a previsão da IEA para a demanda mundial de petróleo foi sendo reduzida ao longo de 2026.

Emissões em trajetória de aumento — Foto: Arte/g1

Em janeiro, a agência ainda projetava aumento de aproximadamente 930 mil barris por dia . Em setembro, a estimativa já apontava para uma demanda 2,5 milhões de barris por dia menor que a de 2025.

No gás, o movimento foi semelhante. A previsão de crescimento feita no início do ano deu lugar a uma expectativa de queda no consumo.

O carvão, no entanto, mostra o limite dessa mudança. A IEA prevê aumento de 1,2% no consumo mundial em 2026, para um recorde de 8,94 bilhões de toneladas , já que parte dos países passou a recorrer mais ao combustível diante das dificuldades envolvendo petróleo e gás.

Ou seja, a guerra não provocou uma redução uniforme dos combustíveis fósseis. Ela mudou a combinação entre eles.

Angelo afirma que preços persistentemente altos de petróleo e gás podem acelerar decisões que já vinham ocorrendo, como investimentos em eletrificação e fontes renováveis. Mas ressalta que ainda é cedo para saber se essas mudanças serão permanentes.

“Pode causar uma mudança permanente nos mercados de energia, que pode — e o verbo ‘pode’ é importante — levar a um desmame mais rápido dos combustíveis fósseis.”

E há sinais nos dois sentidos. A procura por tecnologias de energia limpa continua avançando em grandes mercados, ao mesmo tempo que países aumentam o uso de carvão e produtores de petróleo e gás mantêm planos de expansão.

A própria IEA prevê uma recuperação da demanda por petróleo em 2027. Isso significa que parte da redução observada neste ano pode desaparecer quando as condições de oferta melhorarem.

A guerra no Irã provocou uma mudança inesperada nas projeções para as emissões globais de dióxido de carbono (CO₂) em 2026. — Foto: Reuters

O histórico reforça essa cautela. Na pandemia, as emissões fósseis globais caíram cerca de 5% em 2020 , um recuo muito maior que o projetado agora. No ano seguinte, voltaram a crescer. Depois da crise financeira de 2008, ocorreu movimento semelhante.

Há ainda outra diferença entre emitir menos e reduzir a quantidade de CO₂ na atmosfera.

Mesmo que a projeção de queda de 0,5% se confirme , o planeta continuará adicionando bilhões de toneladas de CO₂ à atmosfera. O gás se acumula durante muito tempo, por isso uma redução pequena apenas diminui ligeiramente a velocidade desse aumento.

Medições mais recentes mostram essa diferença. A concentração média global de CO₂ chegou a 423,9 partes por milhão em 2024, segundo a Organização Meteorológica Mundial (OMM), cerca de 52% acima do nível pré-industrial.

Em 2026, as medições feitas em Mauna Loa, no Havaí, uma das principais estações de referência do mundo para o monitoramento da concentração de gases de efeito estufa na atmosfera, voltaram a superar 430 partes por milhão durante o pico anual.

articles.title: 'Go to Pakistan': CJP's Abhijeet Dipke on those doing Hindu-Muslim 'divisive' politics

articles.body: MUMBAI: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke on Friday said Hindu-Muslim “divisive” politics would not work in Maharashtra, calling for Hindus and Muslims to stay together.“This country will only move ahead if Hindus and Muslims stay together, and whoever wants to do such politics, let them go to Pakistan and do such politics,” Dipke said while addressing a large gathering at Shivaji Park in Mumbai.His remarks came as the CJP held a protest demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Despite police denying permission for the event, thousands of protesters gathered at the iconic ground on Gandhi Jayanti, with heavy security deployed around the area.Also read: 'Did we ask you to sell tea?': CJP's Abhijeet Dipke targets PM Modi at Mumbai's Shivaji ParkMore than 10,000 people turned up at the demonstration.The protest was part of the CJP's campaign against what the party describes as irregularities in electoral rolls and the functioning of the Election Commission.Dipke also announced that the movement would be taken to Delhi if Kumar did not resign.“If Gyanesh Kumar doesn't resign, cockroaches from across India will march to Delhi & protest at Jantar Mantar on October 10," he said in a post on X, adding that it will be a peaceful agitation and every citizen who wants free and fair elections must join it.Veteran actors Naseeruddin Shah and Shabana Azmi, filmmakers Vishal Bhardwaj and Hansal Mehta, singer-music director Vishal Dadlani and Tushar Gandhi, the great-grandson of Mahatma Gandhi, were among those present at the protest.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Mumbai | Silver Rate in Mumbai | Bank Holidays in Mumbai | Public Holidays in Mumbai | Mumbai AQI | Weather in Mumbai | Petrol Price in Mumbai | Diesel Price in Mumbai | CNG Price in Mumbai | LPG Price in MumbaiStay updated with the latest Mumbai news. articles.title: Machchhar, Hathi, Ghoda: Curious menagerie in Gujarati surnames
articles.summary: AHMEDABAD/MUMBAI: When Captain Smit Machchhar’s name did the rounds as the commander who helped avert disaster on a flydubai flight, the applause came
articles.body: AHMEDABAD/MUMBAI: When Captain Smit Machchhar’s name did the rounds as the commander who helped avert disaster on a flydubai flight, the applause came with a side of curiosity. Machchhar? As in a mosquito, in Hindi? A creature that has clocked more flying hours than any airline pilot, with no licence, no type rating and never once a boarding pass?Machchhar belongs to a small menagerie of zoological and entomological surnames found among Gujarati communities including Nagar Brahmins, Brahmkshatriya and Lohanas, sociologists point outThe list includes Ghoda (horse), Mankad (bed bug), Mankodi (large ant, such as a carpenter ant), Popat (parakeet), Vinchhi (scorpion), Shiyal (jackal), Tetar (pheasant/partridge) and Hathi (elephant), among others.In the Nagar community, one branch of the family tree can buzz while another trumpets. The surname of Captain Manoj Hathi, former director (operations) at Air India, means elephant in Hindi.“The joke wrote itself. I was type-rated on the Boeing 747, colleagues couldn’t resist the joke about Captain Hathi flying the jumbo jet,” said Captain Hathi. “Back then, at Air India, we also had a Captain Wagh and an inflight supervisor named Homi Ghoda, a Parsi.”“In the West, my surname doesn’t attract much attention. In fact, it’s one of the Indian surnames that is easy to pronounce. In UK, people associated my name with Colonel Hathi, a character in Rudyard Kipling’s ‘The Jungle Book’, so they found it easy to remember,” he said. “In India, some people would ask, ‘How come your surname is elephant when you are so thin?’ Now that I’ve put on weight, they say I’ve become true to the name,” he added.Abhilash Ghoda, a Gujarati filmmaker from the Nagar community in Junagadh, said the surname draws attention outside the state. “We wear it with pride. I don’t think many of us know the surname’s etymology, but our family has carried it with elan for generations,” he says.Machchhar is associated with the Brahmkshatriya community in Gujarat, especially in districts such as Surendranagar, said Raju Dubal, secretary of the community association in Wadhwan.Bharti Vinchhi, a resident of Ahmedabad and a member of the Brahmkshatriya community, said such surnames are in a minority. “We were told by our forefathers that our ancestors were experts in treating insect bites, including those of scorpions. Thus, the insect was associated with the community,” she said. “Apart from animals and insects, we also have surnames such as Bhoot (ghost) and Jogi (ascetic).”Gaurang Jani, an Ahmedabad-based sociologist, said the only authoritative work on Gujarati surnames was by Vinodini Neelkanth, a Gujarati author and US-trained sociologist. “Her 1942 book, ‘Gujarati Atako no Itihas (History of Gujarati Surnames)’, still remains an important scholarly work on the subject. She explains the surnames as a possible totem — groups revere a specific animal or identify with the positive traits of an animal and thus get identified with it,” he said.“The concentration of such surnames in the Saurashtra region is to do with the large presence of close-knit communities instead of larger association with castes,” Jani added.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Ahmedabad | Silver Rate in Ahmedabad | Bank Holidays in Ahmedabad | Public Holidays in Ahmedabad | Ahmedabad AQI | Weather in Ahmedabad | Petrol Price in Ahmedabad | Diesel Price in Ahmedabad | CNG Price in Ahmedabad | LPG Price in AhmedabadStay updated with the latest Ahmedabad news. articles.body: NEW DELHI: Former Uttar Pradesh Congress Committee (UPCC) president Ajay Rai on Saturday called himself a “Hanuman” to Congress leader Rahul Gandhi, saying he would continue to follow the party’s national leadership and carry out its political fight regardless of the position he holds."Whatever decision the national leadership makes. They told me to fight Modi, and I fought openly with full strength, and I will continue to fight. So whatever the national leadership decides, I stand by it. I am certainly a 'Hanuman' to my leader Rahul Gandhi; wherever he says, I will be there," he told ANI.Rai also recalled his contest against Prime Minister Narendra Modi in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections from Varanasi. Describing himself as a “simple worker”, he said he had been fielded against PM Modi with the support of the Congress leadership and Rahul Gandhi.Rai made the remarks after the Congress appointed Aradhana Mishra ‘Mona’ as the new UP Congress president, replacing him as part of an organisational reshuffle ahead of the 2027 Uttar Pradesh assembly elections. Speaking to reporters, Rai said he had always followed the decisions of the national leadership and would continue to do so."A simple worker like me was fielded against Prime Minister Narendra Modi. With the support of the top leadership and Rahul Gandhi, we secured 4.6 lakh votes in Varanasi and defeated PM Modi in seven rounds. I thank Rahul Gandhi and the top leadership for their faith in me and extend my best wishes to Aradhana Mishra Mona. I hope she works hard, takes the party forward and strengthens the trust of workers by standing with them against oppression and injustice," he said.Rai said political positions were temporary and pointed to his record as a five-time MLA from Pindra. He said he had worked extensively for people in his constituency and recalled arranging blood donations when required."Positions in politics come and go. I have been an MLA from Pindra five times and have worked extensively for the people, even arranging blood donations through my family when needed. I thank the Pradesh Congress Committee employees, drivers, staff, workers and supporters who stood by me around the clock and helped me throughout my journey across Uttar Pradesh. We have always stood against oppression and injustice wherever it occurred," he said.Meanwhile, Mishra, after taking charge as the new UP Congress president, said the party was ready for the 2027 Assembly elections and would contest them with the INDIA alliance."Today marks the beginning of a new dawn. I express my gratitude to my leadership for entrusting me with this responsibility. This is a big challenge; time is short, and every Congress worker will have to work. Together, we must work with full strength," she said.Mishra also highlighted the Congress’ focus on women’s empowerment, saying, "If there's anyone who is the biggest example of 'Beti Hun, Lad Sakti Hun', it is me."She recalled the party’s decision under Priyanka Gandhi Vadra’s leadership to field 40% women candidates in the 2022 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections."Before this, under Priyanka Gandhi's leadership, we fielded 40% women candidates with tickets in the 2022 elections. It is evident today that the Congress Party has always worked for the empowerment of women," she said."We are ready for the 2027 elections, and the INDIA alliance will contest the elections with full strength. articles.title: Israel elections, West Asia wars & Bibi’s last gambit
articles.summary: The miraculous survival of Israeli passengers on the flydubai flight that saw an attempted hijacking and potential terror plot – thwarted only by the
articles.body: The miraculous survival of Israeli passengers on the flydubai flight that saw an attempted hijacking and potential terror plot – thwarted only by the quick thinking of Indian Captain Smit Machchhar and the passengers – has become the latest hot button issue in Israel’s upcoming Oct 27 polls. Even before the high-altitude drama, the election was shaping up to be a pivotal one, not just for Israel but also the wider West Asia.For, the polls are taking place at a time when US and Iran are still engaged in war – a war Tel Aviv started together with Washington but now seems to have quietly exited – Strait of Hormuz is still not fully open for oil and cargo traffic, and Israel itself is militarily mobilised on four fronts – Gaza, Lebanon, Syria, and West Bank. Plus, these are the first polls since the Oct 7 Hamas attack on Israel that appears to have fundamentally changed Israeli society. Here’s the lowdown on the Oct 27 polls, the key players, and the issues animating Israeli voters.Lion of JudahThe flydubai incident is literally godsent for Netanyahu. He and his Likud Party have been consistently trailing in opinion polls. But ever the political wizard, Netanyahu is approaching the polls on the front foot. He knows the election will essentially be a referendum on his handling of Israel’s security situation since Oct 7. Thus, he is presenting himself as the only leader who can guarantee Isreal’s security. And flydubai just exemplified his long-running narrative that Israel still isn’t safe, there are enemies everywhere, and only a strong leader like him can lead the country.His tactic? Go on the offensive against any hint of criticism of Israel’s policies – be it at the UN General Assembly (where Netanyahu basically delivered a campaign speech defending his govt’s record) or blasting New York mayor Mamdani.In doing so, Netanyahu is using an old political trick: fuse his image with that of Israel. Thus, criticising him would be seen as criticising Israel. But Bibi’s campaign isn’t without headwinds.The ChallengerNetanyahu’s main challenger in these polls is Yashar Party’s Gadi Eisenkot, a former Israeli army chief of staff. Eisenkot was once No.2 to former PM hopeful Benny Gantz. But he launched Yashar in Sept 2025, months after leaving Netanyahu’s emergency coalition formed after Oct 7. The war in Gaza is very personal for Eisenkot – he lost his son Gal two months into the fighting.Eisenkot has sought to build a centrist coalition, consolidating opposition votes, while also indicating openness to those who are part of the Netanyahu coalition. A poll projection, published this week, showed the opposition bloc led by Eisenkot’s Yashar winning 54 seats in the 120-member Knesset. Netanyahu’s governing bloc was down to 50 seats.Can Eisenkot pull off an upset? Difficult to tell. Eisenkot’s coalition, should it perform per the poll projections, will still be short of the 61-majority mark. Netanyahu, in fact, could be betting on this. He rode out a similar situation between 2018 and 2022, when Israel had five elections. That saw Netanyahu repeatedly frustrate the opposition, eventually returning to power with the most right-wing govt in Israel’s history.So, Netanyahu’s strategy is simple. If he is not getting a majority, make sure the opposition doesn’t get one either. This will see Israelis head back to polls, and run the whole thing again. Netanyahu is banking on the fact that people will get tired and conclude there’s no alternative to him.The Arab dilemmaThat’s the other problem for the opposition. The only way it can cobble together a clear majority is with the support of Arab-led parties. However, in the post-Oct 7 scenario, when Israeli society is so polarised, tying up with Arab parties is kryptonite for anyone vying to form govt. Even if there is no formal alliance, any opposition bloc that relies on votes of Arab parties in the Knesset will be meat for Netanyahu. The latter is already questioning the credibility of the opposition to form govt, saying can Israelis really trust a coalition that would potentially need the support of Arab parties.Will the results impact geopolitics? The regional scenario will remain much of the same, no matter who forms the next Israeli govt. At least in the near term. The divisions within Israeli politics are more on internal issues – corruption charges against Netanyahu, establishment of a state commission of inquiry into Oct 7 failures, judicial reforms, mandatory conscription for the ultra-orthodox Haredi, and the high cost of living. Those looking to unseat Netanyahu see the same threats from Hamas, Hezbollah, and Iran. Only their approach may differ, to a moderate degree.What about Israel’s relations with US? This may be the trickiest issue. Following Israel’s post-Oct 7 wars in Gaza, Lebanon, and West Bank, criticism of Israel and Netanyahu’s govt has grown in US, both on the political left and right. Even MAGA supporters are questioning the unquestioned Washington support for Tel Aviv. Netanyahu essentially believes that US has no choice but to back Israel. Washington, long dependent on Israel to carry out its West Asia policy, may finally be looking to pull back, and allow other allies in the region – Saudi Arabia, UAE, Qatar – to play a bigger role. This would mean that the Abraham Accords are not just a template for Arab-Israeli relations, but also a template to balance against Israel in West Asia.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Texas woman kills 4-yr-old daughter, then shoots self dead after losing custody battle to ex-husband
articles.summary: A Texas mother allegedly killed her four-year-old daughter in an apparent murder-suicide, just hours after a court granted primary custody of the child to
articles.body: A Texas mother allegedly killed her four-year-old daughter in an apparent murder-suicide, just hours after a court granted primary custody of the child to her father, who said she was “supposed to come home to him that evening”.Cibelle Savella, 35, was supposed to hand over her daughter, Vivian, to her ex-husband, Aaron Savella, on Tuesday evening. Instead, she fatally shot the child at their Houston home before turning the gun on herself, according to the Houston Police Department and family attorneys.Police were called to the residence at around 5:45pm and found Vivian dead and Cibelle with an apparent self-inflicted gunshot wound on the third floor. She was taken to a hospital but died a day later, police said, the New York Post reported.In a statement released through his attorney Stefani Shapiro, Aaron's family said Vivian was supposed to return home to her father that evening.“Our family is devastated. Vivian was four years old. She was loved without limit by her father, Aaron, and by everyone whose life she touched. There are no words for what has been taken from us,” the statement said.“Aaron did everything the law asks of a parent who is trying to protect his child. He trusted the courts. He followed every order. He waited for the process to work. On Tuesday, a judge placed Vivian in his primary care, and she was supposed to come home to him that evening. She never did,” it added.Cibelle's new husband, restaurateur Greg Kubala, and a babysitter were inside the house when the shots were fired, according to police and local media reports. They are not believed to have been involved in the shootings, the NY Post reported.“There was a custody hearing earlier today that didn’t go well for the mother,” Houston Police Lieutenant Larry Crowson said after the incident.The statement also said that the stories of “fathers who fight quietly, patiently, and within the law to protect their children, their stories are rarely told.”Shapiro said Aaron had never alleged that Cibelle physically abused Vivian but believed the child was “potentially being emotionally abused”.Cibelle, who was originally from Brazil, divorced Aaron in November 2024 after four years of marriage. The couple subsequently became involved in a legal dispute over custody of their daughter.According to court documents cited by US media, Aaron was granted exclusive rights to make decisions about Vivian's care. Cibelle was allowed to spend time with the child only under supervision by a Texas-based organisation.The court also imposed restrictions on Cibelle's involvement in Vivian's school activities and medical decisions. She was ordered to pay child support and contribute to half of her daughter's out-of-pocket medical expenses.According to reports citing court filings, Cibelle was also restricted from speaking to Vivian in Portuguese unless a supervisor present during the visit was fluent in the language. It was not immediately clear why the court imposed the restrictions.The circumstances surrounding the shootings remain under investigation.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Camp David huddle: Trump team discusses Iran war, possible Yemen offensive - report
articles.summary: US president Donald Trump’s top national security aides met secretly at Camp David on Friday for several hours to discuss the war with Iran and the
articles.body: US president Donald Trump’s top national security aides met secretly at Camp David on Friday for several hours to discuss the war with Iran and the Saudi-backed push against Houthi rebels in Yemen, three US officials told Axios.The meeting was not announced by the Trump administration and came as negotiations with Iran remained stalled, with Trump weighing whether to resume major combat operations against Tehran.Vice president JD Vance chaired the meeting, according to the officials. Secretary of State Marco Rubio, Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth, White House envoy Steve Witkoff, CIA director John Ratcliffe and chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff Gen Dan Caine were among those who attended.“Things were decided or at least deeply discussed,” one US official said, referring to the Middle East crisis.The White House did not comment on the meeting.Iran talks and a possible return to combatThe meeting came as Trump faces a decision over the future of the US campaign against Iran.With negotiations stalled, Trump has been considering whether to resume major combat operations. On Thursday, he issued a stark warning over the talks, saying: “Now I have to make a decision: either Iran signs the deal, or it won’t exist any longer.”Trump was asked about his next move on Iran on Friday afternoon while his advisers were meeting at Camp David.“If I told you, you would have a major story,” Trump told reporters. “But you will see. It is working out very well. Iran is not doing well.”The Camp David discussions also covered the escalating Saudi-Houthi conflict in Yemen.Saudi Arabia is preparing a possible offensive against the Houthis and has been urging Trump to support the campaign with US airstrikes.Trump has so far been leaning against joining the operation, although US officials said he could change his position.The meeting was notable because such high-level discussions at Camp David have been rare. A similar gathering took place in June 2025, days before Israel went to war with Iran.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.body: During the first nine months of 2026, Pakistan recorded 1,232 rebel group attacks, according to a report by Islamabad-based think tank Pakistan Institute for Conflict and Security Studies, indicating that a major security crisis is brewing. The number of attacks in Sept reached a 12-year high, with 225 attacks resulting in 545 deaths. Police and military personnel have been the primary targets of these operations, accounting for majority of fatalities.Spearheaded by groups such as Tehrik-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), Baloch Liberation Army, Baloch Liberation Front and alliances like Ittehad Mujahideen Pakistan, these attacks remain concentrated in Balochistan and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, and former tribal areas. Formed in 2025, IMP is the latest threat and comprises three sub-outfits — Hafiz Gul Bahadur group (HGBG), Lashkar-e-Islam and Harakat Inqilab-e-Islami Pakistan.Just last week, over a dozen security personnel were killed and at least 30 wounded in a suicide bombing at a roadside police checkpoint in Dera Ismail Khan district of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province. A week before that around 21 Pakistani security personnel were killed and dozens injured in a powerful suicide bombing and subsequent firing at the police line and intelligence facility in Kohat, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.The surge in Sept represents a 13% increase from 199 incidents reported in Aug, marking the third consecutive month of compounding violence.Balochistan served as the primary epicentre of the escalation, bearing the brunt of the violence with 131 recorded attacks, accounting for more than half of all nationwide incidents. Khyber Pakhtunkhwa followed with 58 attacks, while the former tribal areas recorded 34 incidents, the institute claimed. articles.title: Shannon Burns could claim £76 million from Gitpod after disability discrimination win; tribunal allows former VP to pursue one of UK’s biggest employment compensation claims
articles.summary: Shannon Burns, an American technology executive and former Gitpod vice-president of engineering, is at the centre of a legal battle that could become one
articles.body: Shannon Burns, an American technology executive and former Gitpod vice-president of engineering, is at the centre of a legal battle that could become one of the biggest employment compensation cases in the UK. Recent reports by The Independent, and The Guardian, alongside employment tribunal records, show that Burns is pursuing £76,071,992 from Gitpod after winning a disability discrimination case. The amount has not been awarded to her. The tribunal has only allowed her to continue pursuing the claim. Scroll down to know more...Who is Shannon Burns?Burns built her career in the US technology industry before joining Gitpod, a software company that developed cloud-based tools for developers. Before moving to Gitpod, she worked with companies including Slack and Lyft and became involved in organisations supporting women in technology.She joined Gitpod in late 2022 as vice-president of engineering, one of the company’s senior leadership positions. At the time, her compensation included a £220,000 annual salary and a bonus of about £78,000. Burns had disclosed that she had ADHD and dyslexia. Tribunal proceedings later examined how those conditions affected aspects of her work, including forgetfulness, organisation and processing written information. She had previously received workplace adjustments at other companies.What happened on the Austria work trip?The incident that brought Burns into the spotlight happened during a Gitpod team-building trip to Lofer, Austria, in April 2023. After drinking with colleagues one evening, Burns returned to her accommodation but could not get into her room because she had misplaced her key. Her roommate was asleep and did not respond, leaving Burns unable to enter. She eventually spent the night in a sauna.The incident became part of wider concerns raised by Gitpod’s leadership about Burns’s performance and conduct. She was dismissed in June 2023, roughly two months after the trip. However, the tribunal did not determine that spending the night in the sauna itself amounted to disability discrimination. Instead, it examined whether Burns’s disabilities contributed to the circumstances and conduct relied upon in her dismissal, and whether Gitpod had taken appropriate steps to make reasonable adjustments for her disabilities.Why did Burns win the discrimination case?A Birmingham Employment Tribunal ruled in 2025 that Burns had succeeded in claims involving discrimination arising from disability and the company’s failure to make reasonable adjustments. One important part of the case involved Burns seeking support for her ADHD early in her time at Gitpod. She had raised concerns about feeling overwhelmed and asked about ADHD coaching. The tribunal subsequently considered whether the company had done enough to respond to her disclosed disabilities. Her separate claim of direct sex discrimination did not succeed, according to reporting on the tribunal proceedings.Why is she seeking £76 million?The £76 million figure comes from Burns’s schedule of loss, which sets out the compensation she says she is entitled to receive. A substantial portion relates to projected future earnings. Her case is that the dismissal disrupted a highly paid technology career and that she could have continued earning at a senior level had she remained in the industry. Same Reports say the claim also includes other forms of loss, including compensation connected with the impact of the discrimination. Burns has said she subsequently left the technology sector and has been retraining as a therapist.Why has the £76 million claim become news now?Gitpod attempted to restrict Burns’s potential compensation claim to £1 million. The Birmingham tribunal recently rejected that application, allowing her to continue pursuing the much larger figure.The judge noted that Burns had an unusually high earnings history and said it was too early to conclude that her valuation had little reasonable prospect of succeeding without further evidence. The tribunal has also ordered information relating to Gitpod’s recent acquisition by OpenAI to be disclosed, as Burns holds shares in the company.Has Shannon Burns actually received £76 million?No. This is an important distinction. Burns has been given permission to pursue a claim worth £76,071,992, but the final compensation has not yet been determined. A separate hearing will have to establish what, if anything, she is ultimately awarded.If the full amount were awarded, it would be far above the UK’s current known record employment tribunal award of about £4.58 million. The compensation proceedings remain ongoing, alongside an appeal relating to the earlier tribunal ruling. For now, Shannon Burns’s case is not about a £76 million payout already secured, but about a compensation claim whose final value has yet to be determined. The case will now move toward determining how, if at all, those claimed future losses should be compensated in light of her disability discrimination findings and her claimed loss of future earnings.You use AI every day. articles.title: John Lennon and Yoko Ono once rented a West Village apartment; the building is now a six-storey mansion that sold for $70 million
articles.summary: John Lennon and Yoko Ono once rented an apartment in a West Village townhouse that has since been transformed into a six-storey Manhattan megamansion.
articles.body: John Lennon and Yoko Ono once rented an apartment in a West Village townhouse that has since been transformed into a six-storey Manhattan megamansion. The couple lived at 105 Bank Street in the early 1970s, when the building was still one of two neighbouring townhouses more than a century old. Decades later, developer RoundSquare combined the two properties and rebuilt them into a 40-foot-wide residence designed by Robert A.M. Stern Architects. The completed home, spanning about 13,000 square feet, has now sold for $70 million. The sale made it New York City’s most expensive townhouse transaction of 2026 at the time of its closing.Lennon and Ono rented the Bank Street apartmentJohn Lennon and Yoko Ono rented an apartment at 105 Bank Street in Manhattan’s West Village in the early 1970s, according to Mansion Global, which cited an earlier Wall Street Journal report. The couple’s former home was part of a historic townhouse that stood alongside 107 Bank Street. Composer John Cage and choreographer Merce Cunningham were among the notable residents associated with the neighbouring property. One physical link to Lennon and Ono remains, the spiral staircase in the backyard is the same staircase that once formed part of their apartment. The Bank Street buildings were later acquired by developer RoundSquare, setting the stage for their transformation into one large residence.Two century-old townhouses became one new homeRoundSquare acquired 107 Bank Street for $9.31 million in September 2021 and bought 105 Bank Street for $8.8 million in February 2022, according to property records cited by Mansion Global. The developer then combined the neighbouring structures into a single 40-foot-wide townhouse. Robert A.M. Stern Architects designed the rebuilt property, which was completed in 2025. Rather than preserving the buildings as separate residences, the project created a double-wide home measuring about 13,000 square feet across six floors. The property was listed for $75 million in October 2025 before going under contract in April 2026. It eventually closed at $70 million.The rebuilt townhouse spans six floorsThe new residence bears little resemblance to the modest apartments that once occupied the original buildings. The six-storey home includes six bedrooms, with a primary suite covering about 2,000 square feet. Its central architectural feature is an open, cylindrical staircase with a black balustrade, a Venetian plaster-clad stringer and a skylight above. The house also has several outdoor spaces, including a back garden, as well as a sauna. Mansion Global reported that the Landmarks Preservation Commission approved an eastern-facing window, giving the property exposure on three sides, something described as unusual for New York townhouses. The preserved spiral staircase provides a direct architectural link to the building’s Lennon-era history.The $70 million sale ranks among downtown Manhattan's biggestThe $70 million closing made the Bank Street property New York City’s most expensive townhouse sale of the year at the time. The transaction also placed it among downtown Manhattan’s largest residential deals, although the downtown townhouse record remained $72.5 million, set by a double townhouse on West 11th Street. The buyer’s identity was not publicly available when Mansion Global reported the closing. The Bank Street property had originally been offered for $75 million, meaning the final sale price was $5 million below its asking price. Its journey from two century-old townhouses to a newly designed 13,000-square-foot residence also preserved a small but notable connection to Lennon and Ono.You use AI every day. articles.title: Drew Barrymore’s grandfather once owned this Los Angeles estate; after Tony Scott bought and updated it, the property spent six years on the market before selling to her Charlie’s Angels director for $14.7 million
articles.summary: Some Los Angeles homes accumulate history so naturally that the property itself begins to feel like a Hollywood character.
articles.body: Some Los Angeles homes accumulate history so naturally that the property itself begins to feel like a Hollywood character. This Beverly Hills estate is one of them. Once associated with legendary actor John Barrymore, the sprawling Spanish Colonial compound has now changed hands for $14.7 million, adding another filmmaker to a property already woven into the story of American cinema, states a report by the Architectural Digest. The buyer is director and producer McG, who famously worked with Barrymore’s granddaughter, Drew Barrymore, on the Charlie’s Angels films, adds the online report.A century of Hollywood connectionsBuilt in the late 1920s by architect John Byers, the estate occupies just under an acre in Beverly Hills’ prestigious Post Office neighbourhood. John Barrymore, one of the celebrated actors of Hollywood’s Golden Age, was once its owner, giving the property an especially notable place in the city’s cinematic history, states the report.The seven-bedroom, 11-bathroom compound encompasses 6,976 square feet across a collection of structures. Rather than relying on a single grand residence, the property is arranged as a small private enclave, with a three-bedroom main house, two guest cottages, a one-bedroom bungalow and a two-storey guest house, adds the report by Architectural Digest.That layout gives the estate the feel of a secluded Hollywood retreat while offering plenty of space for entertaining and hosting guests, the online report adds.Spanish colonial characterMuch of the main residence retains the architectural language of its era, with exposed-beam ceilings, arched windows, French doors and richly detailed interiors. A formal living room features a mural-painted ceiling, while a wood-panelled library is anchored by built-in bookcases and a substantial fireplace.Another standout is the pub room, complete with a bar, dartboard and fireplace, creating a distinctly old-school entertainment space within the home. The interiors are not entirely locked in the past, however. Some of the guest spaces have been updated with a more contemporary aesthetic, including rooms featuring understated concrete walls. The contrast gives the compound a layered quality, balancing its historic Spanish Colonial architecture with more modern touches.Gardens made for entertainingOutside, brick and stone pathways connect the various structures, while loggias provide shaded areas for relaxing. The grounds also include a koi pond, fountains and a kidney-shaped swimming pool, reinforcing the estate's resort-like atmosphere. The property most recently belonged to Donna Scott, widow of filmmaker Tony Scott, who was known for directing films including Top Gun. Scott had acquired and updated the estate, but despite its provenance and extensive amenities, the property remained on the market for six years before finally selling.Now, its next chapter comes with another Hollywood connection. McG, who directed Drew Barrymore in both Charlie’s Angels and Charlie’s Angels: Full Throttle, has become the latest custodian of a house whose history already reads like a film-industry family tree.Images Courtesy: Facebook and Architectural DigestYou use AI every day. articles.title: Philip Rietveld assembled nearly 1,500 acres of Illinois and Indiana farmland over his lifetime; after his death in 2026, his family sold 23 tracts for $22.46 million, with one fetching $32,600 an acre
articles.summary: Over a lifetime of careful acquisitions, Philip Rietveld built a portfolio of nearly 1,500 acres of productive farmland across Illinois and Indiana.
articles.body: Over a lifetime of careful acquisitions, Philip Rietveld built a portfolio of nearly 1,500 acres of productive farmland across Illinois and Indiana. After his death in 2026, his family moved to sell the holdings through a two-day, two-state auction that drew bidders from seven states. The 23 tracts changed hands for a combined $22.46 million, with one 39.9-acre Indiana parcel commanding a striking $32,600 per acre, according to reporting on the sale by Agriculture.com. Read on to know more about it here:A strategic two-state auctionThe sale was handled by Geswein Farm and Land, a brokerage with nearly five decades of experience in agricultural real estate. Rather than listing all the parcels in a single marathon event, the firm split the auction across two days and two states in the first week of September. This approach was designed to give each local market its own moment while keeping the entire portfolio in view as one major regional land event.Johnny Klemme of Geswein said the strategy aimed to reduce buyer fatigue and keep attention focused on the land, according to Agriculture.com. By separating the Illinois and Indiana portions, the company hoped to encourage competitive bidding in each state without overwhelming participants. Klemme described the event as one of the largest in the firm’s history and said the results exceeded even their most optimistic expectations, as per the report.The numbers behind the saleIn total, 1,477.5 acres sold for $22,458,078, producing a combined average of $15,200 per acre across the portfolio. The Illinois side included 15 tracts covering 856.84 acres, which generated 197 bids and brought $9,479,881, or about $11,064 per acre. Prices on those parcels ranged from $8,600 to $16,100 per acre, reflecting differences in location, size, and soil productivity.The Indiana portion was smaller in acreage but far more intense in bidding activity. Eight tracts totaling 620.72 acres attracted 539 bids and sold for $12,978,197, or roughly $20,908 per acre.Individual Indiana prices ranged from $16,600 to the headline $32,600 per acre. Klemme noted, as per the report, that every Indiana tract sold at the high end of what the team had anticipated, with the top result standing out even in a strong market.Who bought the landThe auction drew 82 registered bidders from Florida, Illinois, Indiana, Iowa, Maryland, North Carolina, and Washington. Despite the national interest, no institutional investors purchased any of the tracts. One regional land investment group acquired property on the Illinois side, while the remaining buyers were largely local or regional farmers and landowners looking to expand their operations or secure long-term assets, as per the report. In the end, 13 buyers purchased the 15 Illinois tracts, and just two buyers acquired all eight Indiana tracts. Klemme said these were mostly regional participants who understood the local landscape and were willing to bid aggressively, the report suggested. Their knowledge of nearby development, rezoning potential, and farm performance likely influenced how they valued each parcel.The man behind the portfolioThe land was held in the Philip Rietveld Trust. According to Klemme, Rietveld assembled the holdings over his lifetime before passing away earlier in 2026. Though he did not farm the ground himself, he was intentional about where he bought and had a clear sense of what made a high-quality farm. His tenants maintained the properties well, many of them renting the same fields for years, according to the report by Agriculture.com.The farms shared several attractive features, including paved road frontage, locations near towns, and similar soil profiles and productivity indexes. That consistency made the portfolio easier to market as a cohesive set of assets while still allowing each tract to be evaluated on its own merits. For buyers, the combination of location, maintenance and soil quality made for an attractive package.Why prices were so highAccording to the report by Agriculture.com, Klemme said fundamentals such as strong locations, well-maintained fields and productive soils were key reasons for the sale’s performance. He also cited less tangible factors, such as local knowledge about future development or nearby land-use changes that may not be as obvious to outsiders. In transitional areas, farmland values are not always based on traditional agricultural economics alone. Buyers often view farmland through multiple lenses, including farm expansion, income generation, inflation protection, long-term wealth preservation, development potential and legacy ownership. Unlike many other assets, farmland is finite, which adds to its appeal for families seeking to build or preserve wealth across generations. Klemme noted that each sale represents the closing of one family’s chapter and the start of another’s.How the sale compares to statewide averagesThe Rietveld farms sold above statewide averages in both Illinois and Indiana. According to the National Agricultural Statistics Service, Illinois farm real estate averaged $9,250 per acre in 2026, up 3.6 percent from the previous year and marking the sixth consecutive year of at least a 2.4 percent annual increase. The Illinois tracts in this auction, with prices from $8,600 to $16,100 per acre, sat at or above that benchmark depending on location and quality. In Indiana, Purdue University’s Farmland Values and Cash Rent Survey showed more mixed results in 2026. Top-quality farmland averaged $14,909 per acre, up slightly from 2025, while average-quality and poor-quality land saw modest declines. The Indiana tracts in the Rietveld sale, ranging from $16,600 to $32,600 per acre, traded well above those statewide figures, reflecting their proximity to Chicago, strong soils, and competitive local demand.A legacy that changes handsFor the Rietveld family, the auction marked the end of a long chapter in which Philip Rietveld carefully built a geographically balanced portfolio of Midwestern farmland. For the buyers, it represented an opportunity to acquire well-located, productive ground in a market where supply is limited and demand remains firm. The sale underscores how farmland continues to function as both a working asset and a store of value for families and investors alike.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: A Pennsylvania man started welding old car parts into sculptures in 1988; his Erie front yard now has a two-headed dinosaur and rocket ship
articles.summary: A Pennsylvania man named Richard Schaefer began turning discarded car parts into sculptures in 1988, and his roadside front yard in Erie has since grown
articles.body: A Pennsylvania man named Richard Schaefer began turning discarded car parts into sculptures in 1988, and his roadside front yard in Erie has since grown into one of the region's most unusual local attractions. Visitors driving along Hershey Road will spot a two-headed dinosaur, a rocket ship, a bumblebee, a spider and a figure called Automan, all welded together from old engines, brake shoes and other salvaged automotive pieces. Here’s how the collection started, what you can see, and how to plan a visit, drawing on the artist's own family website.How Richard Schaefer started making car part sculptures in Erie, Pennsylvania, in 1988Richard Schaefer is an Erie native who first became interested in auto art in 1988, using welding and fabricating techniques and basic automotive knowledge learned from his father. The attraction was formerly called Dick's Auto Art and is now known as Schaefer's Auto Art.The raw material came from close to home. Schaefer's brother ran a junkyard called Denny's Auto Wrecking, and Schaefer spent a lot of time there, then began bringing car parts back to his own yard to work out how to weld them together. His first project joined the front halves of two Lincoln Continentals.Meet Automan and the two-headed dinosaur: the most famous auto art sculptures in the yardThe Erie News Now reporter was given a personal tour that began with Automan. Automan's body is built from an engine, a transmission and a drive shaft, and his shoes are made from brake shoes, a pun Schaefer clearly enjoys. Over the years, Automan has been dressed as a pirate, as a Halloween scarecrow, and on the day of the visit he was dressed as a golfer.Standing beside him is the two-headed dinosaur. It has spark plugs for teeth, an oil pan for a head and small wrenches for paws.More roadside sculptures made from automotive parts, from the rocket ship to the bumblebee and spiderThe family website lists a bumblebee, a spider, a rocket ship, Automan and the two-headed dinosaur, and adds that there are more. The photo gallery also shows a Volkswagen spider, a yellow helicopter, a car set into the ground, and a suggestion box.Because the yard is a long-running project, what you see may change from visit to visit. Even so, the rocket ship and the dinosaur are the pieces that most often catch the eye of people passing by on the road.Visiting Schaefer's Auto Art at 3705 Hershey Road in Erie: Location, hours and what to knowThe sculptures sit in Schaefer's front yard in McKean Township, at 3705 Hershey Road. The family website gives the full address as 3705 Hershey Road, Erie, Pennsylvania 16506, and lists the hours as dawn to dusk. When a reader asked whether she could bring a child to see the art and whether there were set hours, the family answered that she was welcome and could come whenever. The stop is a must-see destination for visitors to Erie.The family manages the website, email and social media accounts. You can reach them at schaefersautoart@gmail.com, or find them on Facebook and Instagram under the name Schaefer's Auto Art.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: A severely malnourished stray rescued in Mississippi in 2021 became a FEMA-certified search dog; years later, Canyon is 2026 Dog of the Year
articles.summary: A severely malnourished stray rescued in Mississippi in 2021 has gone from months of medical care to working alongside emergency responders in some of the
articles.body: A severely malnourished stray rescued in Mississippi in 2021 has gone from months of medical care to working alongside emergency responders in some of the US’s most challenging disaster zones. Canyon was brought to the Hancock County Animal Shelter after being found as a stray, where he received extensive veterinary treatment before his intelligence and drive caught the attention of a search-and-rescue handler. He was subsequently placed with Category 5 K9, a programme that trains dogs for specialised search and detection work. After extensive training, Canyon earned dual certifications in 2023 for human-remains detection and wilderness operations. He has since deployed to major disasters, including the Maui wildfires, Hurricane Helene and the 2025 Texas floods, while also assisting investigations. The ASPCA has now named Canyon its 2026 Dog of the Year.From severely malnourished stray to FEMA-certified search dogCanyon's story began in 2021, when he was rescued as a stray in Mississippi and taken to the Hancock County Animal Shelter. He was in poor condition and required months of medical care before he was ready for a new chapter. During his recovery, however, those around him noticed that he had qualities that could make him suitable for demanding work.A handler later spotted Canyon's intelligence and drive and helped place him in the Category 5 K9 programme. The organisation works with dogs for specialised search, detection and service roles. Canyon underwent extensive training designed to turn his natural abilities into skills that could be used in real-world emergency situations.The transition required more than simply teaching Canyon to follow commands. Search-and-rescue dogs need to remain focused around unfamiliar surroundings, loud noises, difficult terrain and other distractions. They also have to work closely with their handlers, who learn to interpret changes in the dogs' behaviour as they detect scents.Training prepared Canyon for difficult searchesCanyon's training focused on human-remains detection and wilderness search work. He eventually earned certifications in 2023 through FEMA for Human Remains Detection and through the International Police Work Dog Association for wilderness operations.His physical abilities have also proved valuable during deployments. According to Christy Bormann, Canyon's handler, his size, speed and agility allow him to reach places that may be difficult or unsafe for people. His sense of smell enables him to locate human scent in environments where visual searches alone may not be enough.Texas A&M University has also highlighted the importance of veterinary support for its search-and-rescue canines. Bormann has described Canyon and another working dog, Connor, as family members and best friends, while stressing that their health and safety are essential to their ability to work.From Maui wildfires to Texas floodsOnce certified, Canyon began taking part in major search-and-rescue operations. His deployments have included the 2023 Maui wildfires and Hurricane Helene, as well as the devastating Texas floods in 2025.His work following the Texas floods was particularly extensive. Canyon spent more than 90 days searching along the Guadalupe River near Camp Mystic, where search teams worked to locate victims following the disaster. The prolonged deployment placed Canyon and his handler in difficult conditions as they searched large areas of terrain.Canyon's work has also extended beyond major disasters. Alongside Bormann, he has assisted with missing-person searches and homicide investigations. His specialised detection abilities can help teams search areas where investigators need additional scent-detection capabilities.A rescue dog helping othersCanyon's career has given his original rescue story a striking turn. He entered the animal welfare system as a dog requiring care and rehabilitation. After receiving that opportunity, he became a trained working canine involved in searches for people and human remains.The ASPCA specifically highlighted this transformation when announcing its 2026 Humane Awards. The organisation described Canyon as an example of what shelter dogs can accomplish when they receive a second chance and the opportunity to develop their abilities.For Bormann, Canyon's story also demonstrates why shelter dogs should not be defined solely by the circumstances in which they are found. His intelligence, drive and physical abilities eventually made him capable of performing specialised work in some of the most difficult environments faced by search teams.Canyon named ASPCA's 2026 Dog of the YearThe ASPCA announced Canyon as its 2026 Dog of the Year as part of its annual Humane Awards. The awards recognise both people and animals whose actions have contributed to animal welfare or helped their communities.Canyon is among several 2026 honourees, including miniature therapy horses Aiden and Pearl, Kid of the Year Eloise “Lulu” Peck, farm animal welfare advocate Craig Watts, NYPD Mounted Unit Detective Kyle McLaughlin and Colorado Rapid Avalanche Deployment.The ASPCA's recognition comes after Canyon's years of work in disaster response and investigations. His path from a severely ill stray in a Mississippi shelter to a certified search-and-rescue canine has become the defining part of his story.Award ceremony set for October 8Canyon and the other 2026 Humane Awards recipients are scheduled to be formally recognised at the ASPCA Humane Awards luncheon at The Plaza Hotel in New York City on October 8, 2026.Bormann has said she expects to continue working with Canyon for about two more years before he retires from operational work. After that, the search dog is expected to enjoy a quieter life away from disaster deployments.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: A Florida owner planned 52 ten-acre homesites across his 625-acre cattle ranch if the county would not buy it; after two years of talks, officials agreed to pay $7.8 million and stop the development
articles.summary: A 625-acre cattle ranch in Collier County, Florida, is set to take a different path after county officials agreed to move forward with its acquisition
articles.body: A 625-acre cattle ranch in Collier County, Florida, is set to take a different path after county officials agreed to move forward with its acquisition rather than see the property move towards a large-lot residential development. According to Gulfshore Business, the county agreed to pursue the property for about $7.8 million following roughly two years of negotiations with its owner. The acquisition is intended to prevent plans for 52 ranchettes, each covering about 10 acres, along Oil Well Road. A 2023 Collier County Conservation Collier Initial Criteria Screening Report found that Wildflowerz Ranch scored 331 out of 400 in the county’s conservation assessment, reflecting its ecological value, wildlife habitat and connectivity.Ranch was facing a 52-lot developmentWildflowerz Ranch is located along Oil Well Road, east of State Road 29, in eastern Collier County. The property stretches across both the northern and southern sides of the road and has historically been used as a cattle ranch. The development possibility involved dividing the land into 52 ranchettes, with each parcel covering roughly 10 acres. A 2024 real estate advertisement promoted 10.1-acre lots at the property, with asking prices ranging from $289,000 to $479,000.At a September 22 public hearing, attorney Rich Yovanovich, representing the owner, told the Board of County Commissioners that the preference was for Conservation Collier to acquire the property. If the county did not proceed, he said, the owner would move forward with development. That prospect became an important part of the county’s consideration as officials weighed whether to acquire the ranch through its Conservation Collier land-acquisition programme.Two years of negotiations preceded the dealThe proposed acquisition followed a lengthy series of negotiations and changing appraisals. County records show that in September 2024, Collier County offered $6,700,500 for the property, based on the acquisition policy then in effect at that time. By December 2025, two new appraisals valued the land at $7.03 million and $7.99 million. In January 2026, county officials offered $7.03 million, representing the lower of those two appraisals under the policy in place at the time. The owner rejected that offer and countered at $12.8 million. The county later proposed $7.445 million for approximately 634 acres, using the average of the two appraisals.The revised purchase price was set at $7,813,564.70, after the owner agreed to convey an additional 14 acres to Lee County Electric Cooperative. Commissioners unanimously directed county staff to pursue the acquisition at that revised price. The county's current policy had moved to using the lower of two independent appraisals, which was $7.03 million. However, commissioners agreed to the higher purchase price, closer to the $7.99 million appraisal, citing the environmental value of the property.Why the land attracted conservation interestThe ranch's development potential was only one part of the discussion. County officials also assessed the property's natural features and its position within a wider network of conservation lands. The property is within the Big Cypress Area of Critical State Concern and the Rural Land Stewardship Area Overlay. It is also adjacent to conservation lands and lies within the Okaloacoochee Slough, a freshwater wetland system covering about 32,000 acres across Collier and Hendry counties.The county's screening report identified freshwater marshes, pine flatwoods, scrubby flatwoods and mixed wetland hardwoods on the property. The land also provides habitat for a range of wildlife, including wading birds, caracara, gopher tortoises, Big Cypress fox squirrels and bonneted bats. Telemetry has recorded Florida panthers in the surrounding area.The Conservation Collier assessment awarded the property 331 of a possible 400 points. Its ecological value and ecosystem connectivity were among the strongest components of the assessment, while the report also evaluated human value, restoration and management potential, and vulnerability to future changes.Cattle operation will continue for nowThe purchase will not immediately end the ranch's agricultural use. Commissioners also agreed to extend the existing cattle lease on the property through December 31, 2027. The ranch contains fencing, a cattle pen and chute area, a pole barn, a shooting berm and a covered shooting area. The September 22 county meeting agenda formally listed the Wildflowerz Ranch acquisition as an item concerning the proposed purchase through the Conservation Collier programme, including the proposed exclusion of approximately 14 acres for conveyance to Lee County Electric Cooperative. The ranch therefore remains an active agricultural property even as its longer-term direction shifts towards conservation ownership.From potential homesites to protected landThe Wildflowerz Ranch deal illustrates how the county's land-acquisition programme can be used when privately owned property has both development potential and conservation value. Since Conservation Collier began in 2003, the programme has acquired more than 6,672 acres, according to Gulfshore Business. Its stated purposes include protecting water quality and wildlife habitat while creating opportunities for recreation and access to preserved land.For Wildflowerz Ranch, the proposed acquisition would prevent what could have become a 52-lot development and place the property under county ownership for conservation purposes. The proposed $7.8 million acquisition is also paired with an extension of the existing cattle lease through the end of 2027 while the county determines the property's longer-term management and use.You use AI every day.
